passage: Baljeet was on the late shift at the sports club reception when she noticed Kiran's phone in the lost-and-found basket; her daughter had come for swimming and forgotten it. As Baljeet picked it up, the screen lit with a message: "lol ur mom still thinks we were at Simran's on Saturday??" Baljeet sat down slowly. Saturday. Kiran had said she was studying at Simran's house. She had even sent a photo of textbooks. Baljeet's hands went cold. She thought of the tuition class Kiran said she attended, the pocket money for "project supplies", the new friend she'd never met. Were those lies too? A member came to the counter to ask about locker keys. Baljeet heard herself answer, from very far away.

qa.q: Where had Kiran said she was on Saturday?
qa.a: She had said she was studying at Simran's house.

qa.q: What is Baljeet afraid might also be lies after reading the message?
qa.a: She starts doubting everything Kiran has told her, even the tuition class, the money for project supplies and the new friend.

qa.q: What could Baljeet do before talking to Kiran that evening?
qa.a: She could let the shock settle and plan to start by asking why Kiran felt she had to lie, rather than listing every possible lie.

qa.q: What would change if Baljeet decided every past story was false?
qa.a: Kiran might feel that even true things aren't believed, which could push her to hide more instead of opening up.

grounding: Shows a mother who discovers from her daughter's phone that she lied, feeling shock and hurt and starting to doubt even true things.

passage:
Santosh bhai,
I need to tell someone, and you're the only one who won't lecture me. Last night Pari's phone buzzed on the dining table while she was in the shower. The message said, "Don't worry, ur parents will never know abt the movie." The "group study" she told us about on Sunday was a movie at the mall with people I've never met. I sat there shaking. Then I started going backwards. The science workshop? The extra class on Thursdays? Was any of it real? I'm her mother, and suddenly I feel like I don't know her. I can't stop doubting even the things I know are true. I haven't said anything to her yet. I'm scared of what I'll say.
Hansa

qa.q: What did the message on Pari's phone say?
qa.a: It said, "Don't worry, ur parents will never know abt the movie."

qa.q: What is Hansa scared of?
qa.a: She is scared of what she will say to Pari while she is this hurt and shaken.

qa.q: What is a wise first step for Hansa before talking to Pari?
qa.a: Let the shock settle, talk it through with someone calm like Santosh, then go to Pari to understand why she lied, not to accuse her of everything.

qa.q: How might Pari feel if her mother questioned every past outing at once?
qa.a: Pari might feel that nothing she says will be believed, which could make her defensive or more secretive.

grounding: Shows a mother finding messages that reveal her daughter's lie, reeling with hurt and doubting everything, even things she knows are true.

passage:
Dear Susan,

I need to tell someone, and you're my sister, so it's you.
Last night Gopika left her phone on the dining table and it lit up. A message from her friend: "Last night at the beach party was amazing! Did your mum ever find out?" She had told me she was at Anjali's house studying for the chemistry test.
I felt the floor tilt. I read it three times. I didn't sleep.
And now I keep going back. Was she really at tuition on Tuesdays? Did she really go to the library last month? Things that were probably true now feel suspicious.
She's my daughter. How do I trust anything she says?

Elizabeth

qa.q: Where did Gopika say she had been?
qa.a: At Anjali's house, studying for the chemistry test.

qa.q: What was Elizabeth feeling after reading the message?
qa.a: She was shocked and hurt, the floor tilting, and began to doubt everything Gopika had told her, even things that were likely true.

qa.q: What turning point is available to Elizabeth now?
qa.a: She could wait until she is calmer and then ask Gopika directly about the beach party, hoping to understand before deciding what to believe.

qa.q: What might Gopika be experiencing, if she knows her mother saw the message?
qa.a: She is probably anxious and ashamed, and afraid of what her mother will do.

grounding: A mother writes to her sister after finding messages showing her daughter lied, describing shock, hurt and doubt about everything.

passage:
Ritu, I have to tell you what happened, because I'm going mad. I'm Jasleen, and I found out my daughter lied to me.
She said she was sleeping over at Simar's house on Saturday. And then Sunday morning I was checking her phone to find a photo for her school form, and there it was. A group chat. Photos. A concert in the city. Midnight.
I sat on her bed and just shook. Shock, first. Then hurt, deep hurt.
And now my mind won't stop. Last month, when she said she was at the library? Was that a lie? The tuition fees she said she paid?
I don't know what's true anymore. That's what hurts the most.

qa.q: Where did Jasleen's daughter say she was on Saturday?
qa.a: Sleeping over at Simar's house.

qa.q: What was Jasleen feeling after finding the photos?
qa.a: She felt shock and then deep hurt, shaking on her daughter's bed.

qa.q: What turning point is available to Jasleen at this stage?
qa.a: She could take time to calm down, and then talk with her daughter to learn why she lied, instead of letting doubt spread to everything.

qa.q: What might Jasleen's daughter be experiencing if she finds out her mother knows?
qa.a: She would probably feel scared and guilty, and worried about losing her mother's trust.

grounding: A mother discovers her daughter lied about a concert and describes her shock, hurt and doubt about everything the daughter has said.

passage:
Friday: Sanjana said she was at a friend's house for a project. Yamini believed her; why wouldn't she?
Saturday: Sachin, her husband, handed Yamini their daughter's phone. "It keeps buzzing, she left it in the car." On the screen: "The mall was so fun last night! Your mom totally believed the project thing." Yamini felt the blood leave her face.
Monday: She couldn't stop checking. The tuition class Sanjana said she'd been to. The walk to the library. Were those true? Yamini caught herself watching her daughter over breakfast like a stranger.

qa.q: What did Sanjana say she was doing on Friday?
qa.a: She said she was at a friend's house for a project.

qa.q: What was Yamini feeling when she saw the message?
qa.a: She was shocked and hurt; the blood left her face.

qa.q: What turning point is available to Yamini on Monday?
qa.a: She could calmly tell Sanjana what she saw and ask why she lied, instead of silently doubting everything.

qa.q: What might Sanjana be experiencing at breakfast, if she senses her mother watching?
qa.a: She may feel uneasy and guilty, sensing something has changed without knowing what her mother knows.

grounding: Over a few days, a mother discovers her daughter lied, feels shock and hurt, and starts doubting even things that were true.

passage:
Santosh, your Chandrika Nani will tell you about the worst evening I had as a mother. Your Ma was fifteen then.

She'd said she was at Rupa's house doing a project. I believed her. Then, while charging her phone, I saw the messages. She'd been at a mall across the city with a group I'd never met. "Ma thinks I'm at Rupa's lol."

I sat on the edge of her bed and my hands went cold. It felt like the floor had tilted.

And then the worst part. I started going backwards. The science camp last month, was that real? The tuition on Thursday? Even the true things, I couldn't trust anymore. For days I looked at her face and felt I was looking at a stranger.

It passed, eventually. But I have never forgotten how much one lie can shake everything around it.

qa.q: Where did Santosh's Ma say she was that evening?
qa.a: She said she was at Rupa's house doing a project.

qa.q: What was Chandrika feeling after finding the messages?
qa.a: She felt shocked and deeply hurt, as if the floor had tilted, and began doubting even true things her daughter had said.

qa.q: What was the turning point inside the story that Chandrika could reach for?
qa.a: Before deciding on punishment, she could sit with her shock and later ask her daughter why she felt she had to lie.

qa.q: How might Santosh's Ma have felt, at fifteen, when her lie was discovered?
qa.a: She was probably frightened and ashamed, perhaps also resentful, and worried about what her mother would do.

grounding: An elder recalls finding her teenage daughter's lie and the shock and hurt that made her doubt even true things.
